issues.description: The opening leans on stock marketing phrases ('achieve digital transformation', 'innovate with confidence') that don't say anything specific.
issues.found: boost network performance, optimize costs and achieve digital transformation with open source. Get enterprise-grade security and support to innovate with confidence.
issues.recommendation: Swap in a concrete outcome, e.g. "Cut licensing costs and get up to 15 years of security maintenance for your open source telco stack."
issues.whyItMatters: A telco buyer skims the hero first; if it could describe any vendor, they have no reason to keep reading.

styleRef.principle: Content must read as though written by a human expert — not as generic LLM output. Avoid filler phrases, hedging language, and over-formal constructions.

issues.description: Two hype words ('Supercharge', 'cutting-edge') sit on a line that otherwise lists concrete, credible technology.
issues.found: Supercharge your performance and efficiency with cutting-edge technologies such as Smart NICs, DPUs, and GPUs
issues.recommendation: State it plainly: "Improve performance and efficiency with Smart NICs, DPUs, and GPUs."
issues.whyItMatters: Unbacked hype undercuts trust right next to genuinely strong technical proof.

styleRef.principle: Don't add impact with superlatives you cannot justify (e.g. 'cutting edge', 'state-of-the-art', 'best in class'); check your facts and use them sparingly.

issues.description: 'Harness the full potential' is a cliché that adds words without meaning.
issues.found: Harness the full potential of the latest hardware supporting Hugepages and DPDK
issues.recommendation: "Use the latest hardware features, including Hugepages and DPDK."
issues.whyItMatters: Filler phrasing dilutes an otherwise specific, technical sentence.

styleRef.principle: Avoid jargon and long-winded, flowery wording; keep it simple (e.g. 'leverage' → 'use', 'utilize' → 'use', 'facilitate' → 'help').

issues.description: These three reasons are bare fragments with no lead-in and no supporting detail.
issues.found: Improved agility and reduced costs / Experts to help optimize your systems / Long-term support and security updates
issues.recommendation: Add a short lead-in sentence and one concrete proof point under each (e.g. name the support window, or quantify the cost reduction).
issues.whyItMatters: Without specifics they read as generic claims, so a reader can't tell what Canonical actually delivers.

styleRef.principle: We say what we mean using specific, accurate language, and avoid overly convoluted sentences. We prioritize the most important information and present it clearly.

issues.description: The heading is a marketing slogan that doesn't describe what's below it (a list of blog posts).
issues.location: Gain a competitive edge with the latest advances in open source
issues.found: Gain a competitive edge with the latest advances in open source
issues.recommendation: Use a descriptive heading, e.g. "Latest telco engineering articles".
issues.whyItMatters: Readers use headings to navigate; a vague one makes them guess what the section contains.

styleRef.principle: Headings should be sentence case and genuinely describe the content beneath them.

issues.description: The sentence describes a feeling and delays the actual point.
issues.location: Automate operations to lower your total cost of ownership
issues.found: Navigating uncertainty of next-generation infrastructure investment can be overwhelming.
issues.recommendation: Lead with the benefit, e.g. "Automation tools cut the manual work of running next-generation infrastructure, lowering your total cost of ownership."
issues.whyItMatters: Readers scanning the web want the benefit immediately; an abstract opener makes them work to find it.

styleRef.principle: Keep sentences concise and active (subject-verb-object). Get to the point, fast — especially on the web.

issues.description: A statistic appears with no source or date.
issues.recommendation: Add the source and year (e.g. "...in the 2024 Stack Overflow survey"), or move it into an attributed proof-point block.
issues.whyItMatters: An uncited number invites doubt rather than building confidence.

styleRef.section: Security claims, hyperbolic and absolute statements
styleRef.principle: Don't make hyperbolic or absolute claims that cannot be backed up (e.g. 'game-changing', 'revolutionary', 'most secure').
